In applied mathematics, the '''Calderón projector''' is a [[pseudo-differential operator]] used widely in [[boundary element method]]s. It is named after [[Alberto Calderón]].

== Definition ==
The interior Calderón projector is defined to be:<ref name="steinbach2008">{{cite book |last=Steinbach |first=Olaf |date=2008 |title=Numerical Approximation Methods for Elliptic Boundary Value Problems |url=https://archive.org/details/numericalapproxi00stei_284 |url-access=limited |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-0-387-31312-2}}</ref>{{rp|137}}

<math>\mathcal{C}_{\Omega}=\left(\begin{array}{cc}(1-\sigma)\mathsf{Id}-\mathsf{K}&\mathsf{V}\\\mathsf{W}&\sigma\mathsf{Id}+\mathsf{K}'\end{array}\right),</math>

where <math>\sigma</math> is <math>\tfrac12</math> almost everywhere, <math>\mathsf{Id}</math> is the [[identity boundary operator]], <math>\mathsf{K}</math> is the [[double layer boundary operator]], <math>\mathsf{V}</math> is the [[single layer boundary operator]], <math>\mathsf{K}'</math> is the [[adjoint double layer boundary operator]] and <math>\mathsf{W}</math> is the [[hypersingular boundary operator]]; on a given bounded domain <math>\Omega</math> with compact boundary <math>\Gamma</math>.

The exterior Calderón projector on a complementary domain <math>\Omega^c = \mathbb R^n - \Omega</math> (taking its interior) is defined to be:<ref name="steinbach2008"/>{{rp|182}}

: <math>\mathcal{C}_{\Omega^c}=\left(\begin{array}{cc}\sigma\mathsf{Id}+\mathsf{K}&-\mathsf{V}\\-\mathsf{W}&(1-\sigma)\mathsf{Id}-\mathsf{K}'\end{array}\right).</math>

That is also linked to the interior Calderón projector by <math>\mathcal{C}_{\Omega^c} = \mathcal I - \mathcal{C}_{\Omega}</math>.

== Calderón identities ==

As the Calderón operator is a projector; that means that <math>\mathcal{C}_{\Omega}^2 = \mathcal{C}_{\Omega}</math>, the following identities holds :

<math>VW = \frac 14 Id - K^2</math>

<math>WV = \frac 14 Id - K'^2</math>

<math>KV = VK'</math>

<math>WK = K'W</math>
